parts.prose: monitor the utility services referred to in point (c) and report to the competent internal or external personnel events outside the minimum and maximum control thresholds referred to in point 13.2.2(b) affecting the utility services;[cite: 2]

parts.name: item
parts.prose: conclude contracts for the emergency supply with corresponding services, such as for the fuel for emergency power supply;[cite: 2]

parts.name: item
parts.prose: ensure continuous effectiveness, monitor, maintain and test the supply of the network and information systems necessary for the operation of the service offered, in particular the electricity, temperature and humidity control, telecommunications and Internet connection.[cite: 2]

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
GUIDANCE

* Consider the availability of supporting utilities in the business continuity plan (section 4.1).[cite: 2]
* Consider the availability of supporting utilities, when implementing backup management (section 4.2).[cite: 2]
* Consider implementing measures for the protection of supporting utilities, such as (indicative, non-exhaustive list):[cite: 2]
  * active/passive cooling;[cite: 2]
  * automatic restart after power interruption;[cite: 2]
  * battery backup power;[cite: 2]
  * diesel generators;[cite: 2]
  * backup fuel;[cite: 2]
  * uninterruptable power supply, hot standby power generators;[cite: 2]
  * sufficient fuel delivery SLA;[cite: 2]
  * delivery companies;[cite: 2]
  * redundant cooling;[cite: 2]
  * spare parts for components of network and information systems; and[cite: 2]
  * power backup systems.[cite: 2]

parts.name: evidence
parts.prose:
EXAMPLES OF EVIDENCE

* Description of different types of supporting utilities.[cite: 2]
* Measures to protect against the failure and disruption of supporting utilities.[cite: 2]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The relevant entities shall test, review and, where appropriate, update the protection measures on a regular basis or following significant incidents or significant changes to operations or risks.[cite: 2]

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
GUIDANCE

* Conduct routine tests of protection measures.[cite: 2]
* Set up periodic reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of current protection measures.[cite: 2]

parts.name: evidence
parts.prose:
EXAMPLES OF EVIDENCE

* Updated measures to protect against the failure and disruption of supporting utilities, review comments and/or change logs.[cite: 2]
* Evidence that the measures that protect supporting utilities against failures and disruptions are deployed and regularly tested.[cite: 2]

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
GUIDANCE TIPS

* Include a simulated total power failure in the verification of the testing procedure for power generators.[cite: 2]
* Make employees aware of dependencies on supporting utilities.[cite: 2]
* Train staff in how to respond effectively to failures and disruptions of supporting utilities.[cite: 2]
* Set up monitoring systems to detect utility failures or disruptions.[cite: 2]

parts.name: evidence
parts.prose:
EXAMPLES OF EVIDENCE (TIPS)

* Records of internal communications, emails or newsletters highlighting the importance of supporting utilities and their impact on operations.[cite: 2]
* Logs demonstrating detection and recording of any utility failures or disruptions.[cite: 2]

groups.title: 13.2 PROTECTION AGAINST PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL THREATS

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the purpose of Article 21(2)(e) of Directive (EU) 2022/2555, the relevant entities shall prevent or reduce the consequences of events originating from physical and environmental threats, such as natural disasters and other intentional or unintentional threats, based on the results of the risk assessment carried out pursuant to point 2.1.[cite: 2]

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
GUIDANCE

* Consider risks associated with current and forecasted physical and environmental threats to the network and information systems, where relevant (108).[cite: 2]
  * Include in the assessment the (physical) locations of the entity’s facilities.[cite: 2]
* Based on the results of the risk assessment determine the assets that need to be protected from physical and environmental threats.[cite: 2]

parts.name: evidence
parts.prose:
EXAMPLES OF EVIDENCE

* Risk assessment report that includes:[cite: 2]
  * identification and evaluation of physical locations, such as data centres, offices and server rooms,[cite: 2]
  * analysis of potential physical and environmental threats and[cite: 2]
  * mapping of critical assets to physical locations.[cite: 2]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For that purpose, the relevant entities shall, where appropriate:[cite: 2]

parts.name: item
parts.prose: design and implement protection measures against physical and environmental threats;[cite: 2]

parts.name: item
parts.prose: determine minimum and maximum control thresholds for physical and environmental threats;[cite: 2]

parts.name: item
parts.prose: monitor environmental parameters and report to the competent internal or external personnel events outside the minimum and maximum control thresholds referred to in point (b).[cite: 2]

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
GUIDANCE

* Implement measures against physical and environmental threats.[cite: 2] Parameters to consider are (indicative, non-exhaustive list):[cite: 2]
  * network and information systems in scope;[cite: 2]
  * purpose and scope;[cite: 2]
  * description of facilities;[cite: 2]
  * roles and responsibilities;[cite: 2]
  * management commitment;[cite: 2]
  * coordination among organisational units;[cite: 2]
  * compliance with national and EU law, including personal data protection.[cite: 2]
* Consider potential physical and environmental threats relevant to the context, location and operational environment.[cite: 2] The following list offers examples (indicative and non-exhaustive) to support risk-based planning:[cite: 2]
  * fire, flood or natural events (e.g. earthquakes, storms);[cite: 2]
  * public disturbances or unauthorized access, theft or vandalism;[cite: 2]
  * hazardous material incidents (e.g. chemical spills);[cite: 2]
  * long-term environmental changes (e.g. climate trends, air quality).[cite: 2]
* Consider measures against physical and environmental threats such as (indicative, non-exhaustive list):[cite: 2]
  * physical access control measures (e.g. IDs, badges, logs; visitor management system and physical barriers);[cite: 2]
  * surveillance systems (e.g. CCTV, entry points, exits, locking mechanisms and security personnel);[cite: 2]
  * climate control (e.g. temperature and humidity controls and HVAC systems);[cite: 2]
  * fire prevention and response measures (e.g. fire alarms, smoke detectors, sprinkler systems and fire extinguishers);[cite: 2]
* Consider enhanced (maximum) measures to be activated during heightened threat levels or specific scenarios.[cite: 2] Examples of such measures include (indicative, non-exhaustive list):[cite: 2]
  * Increased security personnel, advanced biometric access controls and lockdown procedures.[cite: 2]
  * Enhanced monitoring systems, redundant power supplies and advanced environmental sensors.[cite: 2]

parts.name: evidence
parts.prose:
EXAMPLES OF EVIDENCE

* Detailed documentation showing the design and implementation of measures against physical and environmental threats.[cite: 2]
* Reports outlining the defined minimum and maximum control thresholds for various threats.[cite: 2]
* Logs from environmental monitoring systems showing continuous tracking of parameters, such as temperature, humidity and security breaches.[cite: 2]
* Records of incidents where parameters fell outside the defined thresholds, including the actions taken and notifications sent to relevant personnel.[cite: 2]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The relevant entities shall test, review and, where appropriate, update the protection measures against physical and environmental threats on a regular basis or following significant incidents or significant changes to operations or risks.[cite: 2]

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
GUIDANCE

* Schedule and perform regular tests, such as quarterly fire drills and annual assessments of physical security measures.[cite: 2]
  * Conduct both announced and unannounced tests.[cite: 2]

parts.name: evidence
parts.prose:
EXAMPLES OF EVIDENCE

* Detailed reports of the tests conducted, including objectives, procedures, results and any issues identified.[cite: 2]
* Minutes from review meetings detailing discussions, findings and decisions regarding protection measures.[cite: 2]

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
GUIDANCE TIPS

* Consider creating a topic-specific policy for protection against physical and environmental threats.[cite: 2]
* Deploy periodic simulations and awareness raising activities to assess the readiness of personnel and the adequacy of the procedures.[cite: 2]
* Consider implementing physically secure storage facilities for high-criticality assets of.[cite: 2]

parts.name: evidence
parts.prose:
EXAMPLES OF EVIDENCE (TIPS)

* Documented physical and environmental security policy, including a description of facilities and network and information systems in scope.[cite: 2]
* Results of periodic simulations and awareness raising activities.[cite: 2]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the purpose of Article 21(2)(i) of Directive (EU) 2022/2555, the relevant entities shall prevent and monitor unauthorised physical access, damage and interference to their network and information systems.[cite: 2]

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
GUIDANCE

* Implement perimeter physical access control, where relevant (109), taking into account the measures for protection against physical and environmental threats (section 13.2).[cite: 2]
* Ensure that physical access control is integrated with logical and network access control, in line with human resources security procedures (section 10.1) to support the detection of irregular activities and enhance overall organisational security.[cite: 2]

parts.name: evidence
parts.prose:
EXAMPLES OF EVIDENCE

* Documented policy for physical security measures, including a description of facilities and network and information systems in scope.[cite: 2]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For that purpose, the relevant entities shall:[cite: 2]

parts.name: item
parts.prose: on the basis of the risk assessment carried out pursuant to point 2.1, lay down and use security perimeters to protect areas where network and information systems and other associated assets are located;[cite: 2]

parts.name: item
parts.prose: protect the areas referred to in point (a) by appropriate entry controls and access points;[cite: 2]

parts.name: item
parts.prose: design and implement physical security for offices, rooms and facilities;[cite: 2]

parts.name: item
parts.prose: continuously monitor their premises for unauthorised physical access.[cite: 2]

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose:
GUIDANCE

* In the risk assessment, consider risks associated with unauthorised physical access to, damage to and interference with network and information systems.[cite: 2]
* Based on the results of the risk assessment, determine appropriate perimeter and physical access control measures.[cite: 2]

parts.name: evidence
parts.prose:
EXAMPLES OF EVIDENCE

* Documented security perimeters and physical security designs.[cite: 2]
* Records of physical access controls, visitor logs, and monitoring alerts.[cite: 2]
